observations.statement: Useful history references: pooling adds 0.005222499224244892 AUC over static; target-aware DIN-style pooling adds 0.0031358724110027714 over simple pooling. Both lower Logloss. This does not isolate a field or behavior bottleneck.

Full behavior-count correction loses AUC and worsens Logloss for both pooling and DIN. Half correction improves pooling but still loses DIN AUC and Logloss. A discriminating weaker-strength follow-up was tried; these are successful executions with negative scientific outcomes. No combined count/product experiment exists.

The round-3 joint product restriction improves AUC by 0.001162954694291618 versus its ordinary adapter. Cross removal alone helps both metrics; context removal adds AUC with a Logloss penalty. AUC interaction is subadditive. Round-4 replay and inline implementations retain the gains. The ordinary-adapter offset from historical DIN persists; reproduction does not identify its cause.

Aligned unit products improve AUC by 0.0004876567525730069 and Logloss by -0.00012701821779648181 over aligned raw products. Aligned versus crossed replacements favor alignment in raw, unit/full-gradient and unit/detached-gradient settings. Norm-matched forward directions still differ; this does not isolate semantic alignment from representation/optimization.

Earlier projection AUC contrasts are positive at scale 1, event inverse norm, and constant .2, with strongly different magnitudes. Moderate constant scaling attains the adaptive full-rule AUC numerically, while the loss ranking favors full. The earlier adaptive-superiority explanation requires qualification.

Latest full replay exactly retains AUC 0.6149816911798147 and Logloss 0.19656340759133067; constant replay retains AUC 0.6149888455418249 and Logloss 0.1965762552803662. Both exactly reproduce all 23 prior slices. These are seed-42 bridges, not new random initializations.

Within-history scale reassignment has AUC 0.6147298332575719: -0.0002518579222428041 versus full, with Logloss worse by 0.00002158888593131736. It loses AUC in 22/23 overlapping reported slices; length 17-64 is the exception. The intervention is scientifically negative at this seed, not an execution failure.

History-mean scaling has AUC 0.6149872680212398: +0.000005576841425103396 versus full, -0.0000015775205850498963 versus constant. It worsens Logloss by 0.00004208375258465957 versus full. Mean beats reassignment in AUC by 0.0002574347636679075 but has worse Logloss by 0.000020494866653342214. Neither a new practical winner nor equivalence is established.

The latest diagnostic sample has 512 ordered impressions, 60475 regular valid events, 4 empty histories, 508 eligible rows, and only one singleton row. It reports zero same-state full/active product and logit differences, zero padding mass and empty summaries, and weight-sum error at most 1.7881393432617188e-7. No natural floored/boundary events occur. Reported synthetic VJP relative/scaled errors are at most 3.601953077337613e-15; these are candidate-supplied checks, not an independent audit of every training update.

At the reassigned checkpoint, within-history inverse-norm SD is 0.046375468373298645 and own/reassigned correlation is -0.0865853950381279. Reassignment changes own scales by mean absolute 0.05087236315011978 and preserves row scale sums/squared sums within relative errors 1.8293478376563144e-7/1.737557369096976e-7. At the mean checkpoint, averaging changes own scales by 0.03508317098021507 and preserves row sums within relative error 1.0340424694277317e-7. These checks show numerical activity on sampled states, not matched gradient/update energy across trained models.

Mean loses empty-history AUC by 0.00503257408172697 (8272 samples, 310 positives), short-history AUC by 0.0008312016598673866 (41805, 1444), and frequency-1-2 AUC by 0.0033862586845859743 (16534, 1045) versus full. Mean lowers Logloss in only one reported slice. Constant also has subgroup reversals. Shared retraining can change empty-history predictions even with zero empty summary; no per-empty-row causal effect follows.

All 32 authorized trials have detailed receipts, operational success and null errors. No failed host experiment is exposed. Count balancing, unscaled gradients, crossed replacements and reassignment remain as negative or inferior trajectories rather than being erased. Missing sources, tool-output truncation, and unavailable rg are distinct from scientific counterevidence.

interpretations.statement: When heterogeneous event scales are retained, assigning them to different events can harm the observed optimization trajectory. Averaging them instead retains the numerical AUC level at this seed. Correct per-event inverse norm is therefore not uniquely necessary for this observed AUC; harmful reassignment and useful adaptivity are different claims.
interpretations.qualification: One deterministic reassignment and one seed. No semantic relevance, general necessity, sufficiency, equivalence, or repeated-support claim.

interpretations.statement: The full-versus-reassigned difference is a conditional local performance contrast after approximately preserving within-history scale moments. Its interpretation is narrower than a general benefit of adaptivity.
interpretations.qualification: Controlled performance evidence conditional on receipt-described source isolation. Different checkpoints, gradient-direction correlations, temporal/action associations and Adam states remain; no identified mechanism.

interpretations.statement: Moderate product-channel backward scaling or reduced within-history variation is a plausible optimization explanation. The mean and constant replacements weaken the claim that precise event-specific scale assignment is needed for ranking.
interpretations.qualification: Adaptive/full still has the best observed Logloss among the latest four. Tiny AUC differences may be seed/search variation; loss divergence alone does not diagnose calibration.

interpretations.statement: Behavior-count normalization and product-gradient normalization are distinct interventions. Negative count results do not refute all multi-behavior modeling; aligned-product gains do not rescue the abandoned balancing hypothesis.
Earlier projection-by-scale effects remain conditional single-seed evidence. The latest experiment keeps tangent projection and does not independently test projection or interaction.
